title: A Sigil for the Ember
premise: Elodie Eastwick was exiled at nineteen for a storm she swears she never called, banished to the Hollow Valley where magic cannot follow and the last dragon, Vaskar, sleeps out his final centuries. When prayers to the old gods suddenly begin answering themselves across the kingdom of Caelmere — a country that officially no longer exists on any map — Elodie is dragged back into the world by a fugitive priestess carrying a sigil that can open the door between the living land and the dead one. Hunted by the god-emperor's inquisitors and betrayed by the friend who exiled her, Elodie must choose between restoring her stolen power and keeping the fragile found-family she has built. In the end she learns the storm was never hers but the dying gods', and she spends it — all of it — to relight Vaskar's ember, sealing the door forever and choosing belonging over power.
about_author: Coral Sterling is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping river deltas before turning to fantasy. She writes about borders, exile, and the maps people draw around their own hearts from a drafty house near the sea.

chapters.title: The Valley Where Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Ten years into exile, Elodie tends bees and avoids the sleeping dragon Vaskar's crater, until rain falls upward over the valley rim — impossible here. She realizes the ward has cracked. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in longing; the outside world has found her.

chapters.title: A Prayer Answered by Something Old
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A village girl's prayer for rain is answered too well, flooding the valley floor with water that remembers being ocean. Elodie saves the girl and feels, for one heartbeat, her old storm-calling stir. Beat: terror and hunger entwined.

chapters.title: The Priestess at the Gate
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera Ivane, priestess of the drowned god, crosses the valley ward half-burned, clutching a bronze sigil that hums like a struck bell. She collapses at Elodie's door asking for the Dragonkeeper. Beat: desperate hope arriving broken.

chapters.title: What the Sigil Remembers
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The sigil shows Elodie visions: Caelmere burning, gods starving, a door beneath the capital that no longer exists on maps. Sera explains the old gods are answering prayers because they are dying and grasping. Beat: reluctant understanding.

chapters.title: Vaskar Wakes
chapters.summary: Vaskar's POV. The last dragon wakes to find his keeper's descendant entertaining a priestess. Ancient, sardonic, guttering, he confirms the sigil is real — and that opening the door will kill whatever opens it. Beat: dark humor masking grief.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Ash
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Inquisitor Corvin Ashe tracks the sigil's resonance toward the valley, carrying orders from the god-emperor: burn what answers, question nothing. He once loved a storm-caller. Beat: duty grinding against memory.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Inquisitors breach the ward. Elodie, Sera, and the orphaned girl Wren flee through Vaskar's tunnels as the valley burns behind them — the first time Elodie has left in ten years. Beat: grief and vertigo of freedom.

chapters.title: The Road That Isn't on Maps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Through Wren's eyes, the party travels the ghost-roads of dead Caelmere, where milestones bear names no one speaks. Wren decides these strangers are her family now. Beat: fierce, childlike loyalty taking root.

chapters.title: Tolls of the Ghost-Road
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. A bridge demands a memory as toll. Sera pays one of her ordination and lies about which. Elodie notices the gap. Beat: first hairline crack of trust.

chapters.title: The City That Unhappened
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They reach Ondrel, erased from records after the god-emperor's ascension, where citizens live unregistered and free — and terrified. Elodie sees a possible life without power or exile. Beat: temptation of hiding.

chapters.title: Ash Finds Them
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Corvin corners Elodie in Ondrel's market; their history spills out — he testified at her trial. He lets them go, one hour's head start, and hates himself for both choices. Beat: love curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: The Friend Who Exiled Me
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Flashback chapter: the trial, the storm that killed forty people, and Maren — her best friend, now High Warden — whose testimony condemned her. Elodie admits she still doesn't know if she's innocent. Beat: self-doubt as wound.

chapters.title: Maren's War
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. High Warden Maren Voss hunts the sigil-bearer, convinced the returning gods will reignite the war that killed her family. She believes exiling Elodie saved her life. Beat: antagonist rendered sympathetic and certain.

chapters.title: The Ember Falters
chapters.summary: Vaskar's POV. Bound to the sigil's call, Vaskar feels his fire guttering early; the door's pull is draining him. He conceals it, teaching Elodie instead how to hold a flame that isn't hers. Beat: mentorship shadowed by mortality.

chapters.title: Sanctuary of the Unregistered
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Ondrel's council offers sanctuary if they surrender the sigil. Sera refuses for all of them, lying that the group agreed. Elodie confronts her; Sera confesses the god she serves speaks only to her now. Beat: loyalty vs. truth sharpened.

chapters.title: Storm Over Saltmarsh
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Ambushed by wardens, Elodie calls a storm deliberately for the first time in ten years — and it obeys too well, nearly killing Wren. Horrified, she understands why exile might have been mercy. Beat: power as addiction.

chapters.title: What Wren Saw
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, recovering, tells Elodie she isn't afraid of her — she's afraid Elodie will leave them to be powerful again. The words land deeper than any blade. Beat: innocence cutting to bone.

chapters.title: The God-Emperor's Audience
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Corvin reports failure and is granted audience with the god-emperor, who wears divinity like an ill-fitting coat. Corvin realizes the emperor fears the old gods' return more than any rebellion. Beat: the throne shown rotten from inside.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. An old mapmaker in the saltmarsh recognizes the sigil and gives them the true location of the Door of Caelmere: beneath the flooded cathedral of the drowned god — Sera's own order's seat. Beat: revelation recontextualizing everything.

chapters.title: Sera's Cathedral
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera admits she has known the location all along; her god commanded her to bring the sigil there alone. Her faith and her loyalty to the others collide openly for the first time. Beat: betrayal confessed before it happens.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Rain
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Around a marsh fire, each character states what they'd wish of the gods if answered: home, forgiveness, parents, an end. Elodie wishes for nothing — and lies. Beat: intimacy forged under shared vulnerability.

chapters.title: Maren Offers Terms
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren captures Wren and offers Elodie a trade: the sigil for the girl, plus a pardon signed by the emperor himself. Elodie sees the trap and takes it anyway. Beat: sacrifice chosen with open eyes.

chapters.title: The Exchange at Grayford Bridge
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The exchange goes wrong when Corvin, ordered to kill witnesses, turns his blade on his own inquisitors instead. Maren escapes with the sigil; Wren is saved. Beat: Corvin's defection, paid for in blood.

chapters.title: Prisoner of the Wardens
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren studies the sigil and hears it whisper — the gods answering her too, offering her dead family back. Her certainty begins to rot. Beat: corruption of the incorruptible.

chapters.title: Vaskar Descends
chapters.summary: Vaskar's POV. Dying faster, Vaskar attacks the warden stronghold not for the sigil but to buy the others time, and falls, wounded, into the sea. His last lesson to Elodie echoes: spend the fire, don't hoard it. Beat: the mentor's fall.

chapters.title: Ashes and Salt
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Grieving Vaskar, Elodie stops running and plans. If the door needs a storm-caller anyway, let it be her — but on her terms, with her people beside her. Beat: despair transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Drowned God Speaks
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. At the flooded cathedral's edge, Sera's god finally manifests — vast, drowning, less a father than a famine. It demands the sigil and Sera's life. Sera says yes. Beat: faith revealed as devouring.

chapters.title: Into the Flooded Cathedral
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The party descends into the submerged nave, breathing borrowed air from Wren's small answered prayer. Bells ring underwater; the dead congregation still kneels. Beat: awe and horror in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Door Beneath the Altar
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They find the Door: a seam of ember-light in the stone, keyed to the sigil and to storm-blood. Opening it requires a caller to stand in the threshold and hold it. Beat: the cost made explicit.

chapters.title: Maren at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren arrives with the imperial host, sigil in hand, intending to open the door herself and bargain with the gods for her family. The whispering has fully claimed her. Beat: antagonist and protagonist wanting the same door for opposite reasons.

chapters.title: Battle of the Nave
chapters.summary: Ensemble. Inquisitors, wardens, and the awakened dead clash beneath the waterline. Corvin holds the stair; Wren carries the sigil through collapsing arches. Beat: chaos where every alliance bends.

chapters.title: The Truth of the Storm
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At the threshold, the Door shows Elodie the truth: the storm ten years ago was the gods' dying convulsion, channeled through her; Maren knew and testified anyway to save her from the emperor's purges. Betrayal reframed as terrible protection. Beat: devastating clarity.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Water
chapters.summary: Elodie and Maren, face to face. Maren breaks — grief, not malice, all along. She gives Elodie the sigil and takes her place holding the warden line. Beat: reconciliation purchased with ruin.

chapters.title: Sera's Choice
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The drowned god rises to take the Door for itself. Sera, its last priestess, unmakes her own ordination — the memory she never paid — severing its anchor to the world. Beat: faith renounced as the highest act of love.

chapters.title: A Sigil for the Ember
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Climax. Elodie stands in the threshold, calls every storm she was ever owed, and spends it all — not to open the Door for the gods, but to carry its ember-light up to the wounded Vaskar waiting in the deep. Beat: total expenditure, no reserve.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon Relit
chapters.summary: Vaskar's POV. The ember settles into Vaskar's chest; he rises from the sea blazing, and the Door seals behind him with the old gods passing gently through — answered at last, released at last. Beat: resurrection as farewell.

chapters.title: What the Emperor Learned
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. With the gods gone quiet and the sigil spent, the god-emperor's divinity gutters out before his court. Corvin chooses not to save him. Beat: corrupt power collapsing under its own hollowness.

chapters.title: Pardons and Beekeeping
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Aftermath: Maren resigns her wardenship; Corvin plants a garden he's bad at; Sera builds a small honest chapel. Elodie is offered reinstatement as Court Storm-Caller and declines. Beat: gentle comedy of ordinary repair.

chapters.title: The Valley, Rewarded
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The party returns to the valley, wards dissolved by choice rather than decree. Wren plants the toll-memory Sera lost back into her hands as a gift. Beat: belonging chosen freely, wounds acknowledged.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Years later, Elodie keeps bees and teaches valley children weather-sense without magic. Vaskar's glow warms the northern sky some nights. She wanted power once; she got something harder and better. Final beat: peace earned, not granted.
